5: The abstract boardgame known as [Hex][hex] / Polygon / CON-TAC-TIX is quite simple in rules, though complex in practice.
6: Two players place stones on a parallelogram with hexagonal fields.
7: The player to connect his/her stones to the opposite side first wins.

10: Your goal is to build a program that given a simple representation of a board computes the winner (or lack thereof).
11: Note that all games need not be "fair".
12: (For example, players may have mismatched piece counts or the game's board might have a different width and height.)

17: . O . X .

20:    . X O X O

22: ```

24: "Player `O`" plays from top to bottom, "Player `X`" plays from left to right.

// reaches reports whether there is a connected chain of cells of the given
// value that starts on the start side and reaches the end side.
func reaches(grid [][]byte, val byte, rows, cols int, start, end func(r, c int) bool) bool {
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		visited[r] = make([]bool, cols)
	}

	// Seed the flood fill with every matching cell on the start side.
	var stack [][2]int
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if grid[r][c] == val && start(r, c) {
				visited[r][c] = true
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{r, c})
			}
		}
	}

	for len(stack) > 0 {
		cell := stack[len(stack)-1]
		stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
		r, c := cell[0], cell[1]
		if end(r, c) {
			return true
		}
		for _, d := range neighbours {
			nr, nc := r+d[0], c+d[1]
			if nr < 0 || nr >= rows || nc < 0 || nc >= cols {
				continue
			}
			if visited[nr][nc] || grid[nr][nc] != val {
				continue
			}
			visited[nr][nc] = true
			stack = append(stack, [2]int{nr, nc})
		}
	}
	return false
}

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
)

// neighbours lists the six offsets of the cells adjacent to a given cell in
// the canonical (space-stripped) board. The board is a sheared parallelogram:
// each row is shifted one cell to the right relative to the row above it, so the
// legal diagonals are up-right and down-left, while up-left and down-right are
// not adjacent.
var neighbours = [][2]int{
	{0, -1},  // left
	{0, +1},  // right
	{+1, -1}, // down-left
	{+1, 0},  // down
	{-1, 0},  // up
	{-1, +1}, // up-right
}

// ResultOf computes the winner of a game of Hex / Polygon.
//
// The board is a parallelogram of hexagonal cells given as a slice of strings,
// one per row. Cells are '.', 'O' or 'X'; spaces (used for readability and to
// shear the board into a parallelogram) are ignored.
//
// Player 'O' plays from top to bottom and player 'X' plays from left to right.
// The player whose stones first connect their two assigned sides wins. A
// connecting chain of one player forms a barrier that the other player cannot
// cross, so at most one player can win. The result is "O", "X" or "" (no
// winner).
func ResultOf(lines []string) (string, error) {
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}

	rows := len(lines)

	// Strip the readability spaces to obtain the canonical rows and determine
	// the board dimensions.
	board := make([]string, rows)
	cols := 0
	for r, l := range lines {
		s := strings.ReplaceAll(l, " ", "")
		board[r] = s
		if len(s) > cols {
			cols = len(s)
		}
	}

	// Build a rectangular grid, padding any short rows with empty cells.
	grid := make([][]byte, rows)
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		grid[r] = make([]byte, cols)
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if c < len(board[r]) {
				grid[r][c] = board[r][c]
			} else {
				grid[r][c] = '.'
			}
		}
	}

	// Validate the cell values.
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			switch grid[r][c] {
			case '.', 'O', 'X':
			default:
				return "", errors.New("connect: invalid cell on board")
			}
		}
	}

	// Player O connects the top side to the bottom side.
	if reaches(grid, 'O', rows, cols,
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == rows-1 }) {
		return "O", nil
	}

	// Player X connects the left side to the right side.
	if reaches(grid, 'X', rows, cols,
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == cols-1 }) {
		return "X", nil
	}

	return "", nil
}

// reaches reports whether there is a connected chain of cells holding val that
// starts on the start side and reaches the end side.
func reaches(grid [][]byte, val byte, rows, cols int, start, end func(r, c int) bool) bool {
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	for r := range visited {
		visited[r] = make([]bool, cols)
	}

	// Seed the flood fill with every matching cell on the start side.
	var stack [][2]int
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if grid[r][c] == val && start(r, c) && !visited[r][c] {
				visited[r][c] = true
				stack = append(stack, [2]int{r, c})
			}
		}
	}

	// Flood fill (depth first) through the connected cells of val.
	for len(stack) > 0 {
		cell := stack[len(stack)-1]
		stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
		r, c := cell[0], cell[1]

		if end(r, c) {
			return true
		}

		for _, d := range neighbours {
			nr, nc := r+d[0], c+d[1]
			if nr < 0 || nr >= rows || nc < 0 || nc >= cols {
				continue
			}
			if visited[nr][nc] || grid[nr][nc] != val {
				continue
			}
			visited[nr][nc] = true
			stack = append(stack, [2]int{nr, nc})
		}
	}

	return false
}
